# Go template text built from HTTP request data (Go)

`qualor:go/template-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-1336](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1336.html)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Go templates whose text is built from HTTP request data: request data that reaches `Parse` on an
`html/template` or `text/template` template (one made with `template.New`, `Must`, `ParseFiles`,
`ParseGlob`, `ParseFS`, or derived from one with `Clone`, `New` or `Lookup`).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
The Go documentation trusts template authors, not template data. Text passed to `Parse` is
template code: a client who writes it can add actions such as `{{.}}` or `{{call .Func}}` that
read the data given to the template, call its methods and the template's functions, and, with
`text/template`, write any HTML and script into the page.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the greeting is pasted into the template text.

```go
package greet

import (
	"html/template"
	"net/http"
)

func Hello(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	name := r.URL.Query().Get("name")
	t, err := template.New("hello").Parse("<p>Hello, " + name + "</p>")
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "bad template", http.StatusInternalServerError)
		return
	}
	t.Execute(w, nil)
}
```

**Compliant:** the template text is fixed; the name is passed to `Execute` as data, where
`html/template` escapes it.

```go
package greet

import (
	"html/template"
	"net/http"
)

var hello = template.Must(template.New("hello").Parse("<p>Hello, {{.}}</p>"))

func Hello(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	hello.Execute(w, r.URL.Query().Get("name"))
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the template text fixed: a file (`ParseFiles`, `ParseFS` with an embedded file system) or a
  constant.
- Pass request data to `Execute` or `ExecuteTemplate` as data. `html/template` escapes it for the
  place where it appears.
- If users must choose between layouts, map their value to one of a fixed set of templates.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- `net/http`
- `html/template`
- `text/template`
- `encoding/json`
- Gin
- Echo
- chi
- gorilla/mux

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A template is recognised when it is built in the same function or as a package variable, is
  derived from such a package variable, or has a known type (a struct field, a parameter). A
  template returned by a function of another package is not followed.
- HTML-escaping the text first does not help (the template actions survive escaping), so it is
  not treated as making the text safe.
- The binder of the Echo instance is not a source, and numeric struct fields count as safe only
  when the struct is declared in the same file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/go/template/template-injection.go`](../../../rules/go/template/template-injection.go) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
